answer.rationale: Memory b4 documents that circuit breakers on the payments dependency contained a partner outage and preserved the rest of the checkout path by failing fast. The current situation has p99 latency climbing on the write path under heavy settlement load; a circuit breaker on the degraded dependency contains the blast radius, prevents the slow path from consuming all write capacity (thread pools, connections, retries cascading), and preserves customer writes that are still healthy. The security-patched release is not reverted (compliance constraint). Regional failover is tempting per b2, but failover is a large blast-radius move on a latency-only signal with writes already at peak - if the cause is dependency-bound rather than regional, failover shifts the same problem onto the new region. Adding capacity doesn't address a latency-on-write-path regression 90 minutes after a release - capacity wouldn't fix a code/dependency regression. Read-replica routing per b5 is for read-heavy dashboard load, not write-path latency. Circuit breaker is the lowest-blast-radius intervention directly aimed at the write-path latency regression, consistent with prior successful precedent, and leaves the single-intervention window available for escalation if the breaker identifies a specific bad dependency. Cannot verify any memory given the budget; relying on the consolidated record as-is.
